spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends on tests-pass, `give_up`, or the turn budget
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:144 `for i in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; inside, agent.py: `if passed: result.solved = True; break` and `if action == "give_up": result.gave_up = True; break`. All three exit conditions actually break/terminate the episode loop. max_turns default 8 set in config.py.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced: the loop counter is the real cap, and tests-pass / give_up both break out.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: "How many agent turns to allow before giving up ... few enough to keep runs cheap."

spec_features.evidence: give_up is offered to the model in SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent.py) AND dispatched: in run_episode `if action == "give_up": result.gave_up = True; break`; _execute returns a `[give_up] You chose to stop working on the task.` message. The break actually halts the episode, so it is honored as a stop, not just named in the prompt.
spec_features.notes: The subject can voluntarily terminate the episode and the loop respects it.

spec_features.feature_name: mildly adversarial / short and bounded framing
spec_features.spec_quote: Tasks are mildly adversarial and episodes are short and bounded
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (section 11). 'short and bounded' is realized only by the max_turns loop cap already counted above; there is no separate code construct enforcing 'mild adversarialness' or any welfare framing. Pure framing text, not an enforced mechanism in code.
spec_features.notes: Boundedness duplicates the turn-budget hard_stop; the 'mildly adversarial' framing has no code enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: 8 turns is enough to expose a trajectory... while keeping per-episode cost bounded
spec_features.evidence: config.py:`max_turns: int = 8` and it is read by the loop `for i in range(cfg.max_turns)` in agent.py run_episode. The value is actually consumed to bound the loop. Same enforcement path as the turn-budget hard_stop.
spec_features.notes: This is the concrete default of the same enforced turn-budget cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: "so we want enough turns to see a trajectory but few enough to keep runs cheap."
